content:
Warner Bros. has announced it is testing a new format with some iPhone users in the United States: HBO Max Shorts. Vertical video is already annoying enough, and now the media giant says these clips are powered by artificial intelligence tools…

The company stated that the clips are suggested by AI, with human editors making the final decisions.

"HBO Max Shorts" aims to curate memorable scenes from the HBO Max library in a vertical, swipeable feed to help users discover content they want to watch… The clips in this feature are driven by an internally developed AI tool that uses machine learning algorithms and scene-level metadata to sift through thousands of hours of video, recommending the most dramatic and impactful scenes for discovery. After the AI tool suggests clips, HBO Max editors decide which best represent the stories audiences love, then present them in a brand-new vertical video format to ensure smooth playback.

The content is reportedly personalised based on the user's viewing history; if interested in a particular clip, viewers can start watching immediately or add it directly to "My List" from the feed.

Warner Bros. said it is currently testing with a small number of iPhone users in the United States, but appears to have already decided to roll it out to other devices and markets.
